alternatives.option: Replay the admission log verbatim on rebuild
alternatives.reason_rejected: the admission log is per-replica evidence that may be lost; the rule must be derivable from the events themselves
locks policy to the migrator; lane 02c measured and reverted it

context: Lane 02c (migration) delivered on lane/02c-migration: migrate --to 3 / rollback --to 2 / forward recovery per ADR §10 with legacy fixtures, SIGKILL interrupt tests, C21 named tests; part-level projections close C16 L1–L4; two contract gaps and a rebuild/capability defect reported.
rationale: Lane 02c measured rebuild() losing an admitted event (acknowledged_events_lost: 1, rejected: unauthorized) after a membership was added post-migration; seeding a migration policy fixed the rebuild but locked the store's policy to the migrator forever, so it was reverted. Evaluating against the ancestor-projected membership is deterministic, order-independent, and consistent with appendix C interpretation 3 (a membership must be a causal ancestor of anything it authorizes). Assigned to lane 02b (owns admission).
summary: Capability at admission is evaluated against the membership projected from the event's CAUSAL ANCESTORS (the membership event must precede it in the parents graph), and rebuild() replays that same evaluation — never the replica's latest policy — so a policy added later can neither drop already-admitted events nor make admission order-dependent
